docs.title: GridFM App Distribution
docs.text:
GridFM App Distribution provides applications for electricity distribution use cases within the GridFM ecosystem.

The project is at an early stage. Add user-facing guides under docs/manual/ and API/component documentation under docs/components/ as functionality is introduced.

This library is brought to you by the GridFM team to train, finetune and interact with a foundation model for the electric power grid. This library contains specialised tasks for electricity distribution applications.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
This features introduces a new Voltage Loss Detection (VLD) task and the associated model changes needed to integrate it. The goal is to predict post-contingency bus energization status while preserving physically meaningful voltage outputs for buses that remain ON.

This task achieves prediction based load flow simulations in reliability analyses where network contingencies are simulated to identify the customers who are interrupted during each grid failure. This task also guides the model prediction to be topology-aware by guiding voltage predictions for ON buses towards the reconstructed voltage and towards zero for OFF buses.

The purpose of this task to GridFM users is to enforce topology-awareness in distribution networks during contigency analyses. This task is tailored for distribution networks with multiple failures in MV and LV parts.

docs.title: Motivation and Context
docs.text:
The existing reconstruction stack is designed to recover physical power-flow quantities, but it does not explicitly model bus de-energization caused by network failures The VLD task addresses this gap by combining topology-aware supervision with standard physical prediction outputs. This is useful when the model must distinguish between buses that remain energized and buses that should collapse to an off state after a contingency. It also reduces ambiguity in the training signal by making topology the primary driver of status prediction.

Possible use-cases: Reliability assessments, Contigency analysis, Short-circuit analysis, Load flow

Drivers: Acceleration of power flow and short-circuit simulations that involve multiple network contingencies. This is a key research concern as reliability analysis are computationally burdensome when dealing with large network and thousands of contingency scenarios.

Existing issues, discussions, prototypes: Ongoing research has focused on optimising MCS-based reliability analysis for implementation on actual networks currently limited by computational requirements. When combined with MV and LV reliability equivalents, GridFM can enable the accurate reliability assessment of large MV/LV networks using probabilistic methods.

Background material: M. Kisuule, et al., "Topology-Aware Graph Transformers for detecting voltage loss after distribution network failures" IEEE Publication (TBC).

docs.title: Proposed Scope
docs.text:
The intended function of this task is to detect whether a bus survives a contingency while still producing usable physical outputs for the buses that remain active. The model is trained so that topology determines whether a bus can meaningfully carry voltage.

Core functionality: - Add a VLD-specific task that predicts bus status alongside standard physical outputs. - Extend the model so the bus head returns physical outputs plus a status logit. - Use a topology-first loss that treats reachability as the main supervision signal. - Keep physically reachable buses close to their target Vm values. - Force unreachable buses toward zero voltage.

Optional extensions: - Add richer calibration metrics for bus status confidence. - Support alternative topology-confidence weighting strategies. - Add separate reporting for OFF-bus and ON-bus voltage errors.

docs.title: Dependencies and Risks
docs.text:
• The task depends on consistent feature indexing across datasets, transforms, losses, and model outputs.
  • The topology loss depends on latest_x_dict being available during the forward pass.
  • Branch pruning must remain consistent with contingency-specific B_ON handling.
  • The status target layout must match the dataset’s bus target tensor exactly.
  • Changes to grid_path behavior can accidentally overwrite topology state if not handled carefully.

docs.title: Testing and Validation Plan
docs.text:
• Unit / integration tests - Unit tests for feature indices and tensor layouts and Integration tests for the VLD transform pipeline. Loss checks on topology target generation and Vm weighting.
  • Benchmarks: Accuracy compared to topology awareness of power flow solvers in reliability assessments
  • Reproducibility checks: Evaluation of status accuracy, OFF-bus Vm collapse, and ON-bus Vm retention.
  • Real‑world use cases: Distribution reliability assessment

docs.title: Additional Notes
docs.text: This task can be integrated into the Heterogeneous GridFM code stack to guide the prediction of the model's physical quantities with topology awareness.

docs.title: VLDTopologyLoss — tuning parameters and how they guide training
docs.text: This note describes every parameter of VLDTopologyLoss as implemented in gridfm_app_dist/.../loss.py, what part of the objective it touches, what moving it does to the gradients, and how to read the effect on the training curves. Equation numbers refer to Topology-Aware Graph Transformers for detecting voltage loss after distribution network failures (Kisuule, Bessa, Hernando-Gil).

docs.title: 1. What the loss is doing
docs.text:
The model emits, per bus, a status logit \(z_i\) and a voltage magnitude \(\hat V_i\). Two labels exist for each bus:

  • \(y_i^{ ext{reach}}\) — derived in the loss by a breadth-first search over available buses and branches from the energisation sources (eqs. 1–5).
  • \(y_i^{ ext{target}}\) — the dataset's post-contingency energised flag from the power-flow solver.

Four terms are combined (eq. 18):

\[\mathcal{L}_{ ext{VLD}} = \lambda_{ ext{reach}}\mathcal{L}_{ ext{reach}} + \lambda_{ ext{anc}}\mathcal{L}_{ ext{anc}} + \lambda_{ ext{off}}\mathcal{L}_{ ext{off}} + \lambda_{ ext{on}}\mathcal{L}_{ ext{on}}\] Term Supervises Target Per-bus weight Normaliser \(\mathcal{L}_{ ext{reach}}\) (13) \(z_i\) \(y_i^{ ext{reach}}\) \(\omega_i = \kappa_i\,\omega_i^{ ext{cls}}\); 0 on conflict buses \(\sum_i \omega_i\) \(\mathcal{L}_{ ext{anc}}\) (14) \(z_i\) \(y_i^{ ext{target}}\) \( u_i\); \(w_{ ext{off}}\) on conflict buses \(\sum_i u_i\) \(\mathcal{L}_{ ext{off}}\) (15) \(\hat V_i o 0\) buses with \(y_i^{ ext{reach}} = 0\) 1 \(n_{ ext{off}}\) \(\mathcal{L}_{ ext{on}}\) (17) \(\hat V_i o V_i\) buses with \(y_i^{ ext{reach}} = 1\) \(\eta_i = \mathrm{sg}(\hat p_i)\) \(\sum_i \eta_i\)

Each term is a weighted mean, so the \(\lambda\) values compare like-for-like quantities and the batch size does not change their balance.

Two things are fixed by the formulation and are not parameters:

  • Conflict rule. On \(\mathcal{C} = \{i : y_i^{ ext{reach}} e y_i^{ ext{target}}\}\) the topology weight is zero and the anchor weight is \(w_{ ext{off}}\), so the stationary point of \(z_i\) is the label, whether 0 or 1. The voltage terms stay keyed on \(y_i^{ ext{reach}}\).
  • Decision threshold. \( heta = 1/(1 + w_{ ext{off}})\). Weighting the 0-class by \(w\) moves the BCE optimum from the true posterior \(q\) to \(q/(q + w(1-q))\); thresholding at \(1/(1+w)\) maps it back to the boundary \(q = 0.5\). The value is returned as VLD Decision Threshold and must be reused at inference (read \(w_{ ext{off}}\) from the ema_off_weight buffer, which is checkpointed).

docs.title: 2. Gradient picture
docs.text:
For the status logit (eq. 19):

\[ rac{\partial \mathcal{L}_{ ext{VLD}}}{\partial z_i} = a_i(\hat p_i - y_i^{ ext{reach}}) + b_i(\hat p_i - y_i^{ ext{target}}),\qquad a_i = \lambda_{ ext{reach}} rac{\omega_i}{\sum_j \omega_j},\quad b_i = \lambda_{ ext{anc}} rac{ u_i}{\sum_j u_j}\]
  • Agreeing bus, \(y = 1\): slope \(a_i + b_i\) with \(\omega_i = u_i = 1\).
  • Agreeing bus, \(y = 0\): slope \(a_i + b_i\) with \(\omega_i = u_i = w_{ ext{off}}\), i.e. \(w_{ ext{off}}\) times steeper. This is the class balance.
  • Conflict bus: slope \(b_i\) only, with \( u_i = w_{ ext{off}}\); zero at \(y_i^{ ext{target}}\).

For the voltage head (eqs. 24–25):

\[ rac{\partial \mathcal{L}_{ ext{VLD}}}{\partial \hat V_i} = egin{cases} \dfrac{\lambda_{ ext{off}}}{n_{ ext{off}}} ig(2\hat V_i + \lambda_1\,\mathrm{sgn}\,\hat V_i ig) & y_i^{ ext{reach}} = 0 \[1.2em] \dfrac{2\lambda_{ ext{on}}\,\mathrm{sg}(\hat p_i)}{\sum_j \eta_j} ig(\hat V_i - V_i ig) & y_i^{ ext{reach}} = 1 \end{cases}\]

Neither voltage term reaches \(z_i\): \(\eta_i\) is a stop-gradient. The status head is trained only by the two BCE terms.

docs.title: 3.1 Term weights — the \(\lambda\) of eq. (18)
docs.text:
topology_weight (\(\lambda_{\text{reach}}\), default 1.0). Scale of the primary BCE. Acts as the reference the other three are expressed against; leave at 1.0 and tune the others.

target_anchor_weight (\(\lambda_{\text{anc}}\), default 0.5, paper 0.25). Scale of the label BCE. On agreeing buses it only changes how fast \(z_i\) moves (the stationary point is \(y\) regardless). On conflict buses it is the only force on \(z_i\), so it sets how quickly label-only buses are learned relative to agreeing ones. Raised from 0.25 because at 0.25 conflict buses learned four times slower than the rest. Raise further if VLD Conflict Rate is high and VLD Target Accuracy lags VLD Topology Accuracy; lower if the BFS label is known to be more trustworthy than the dataset flag.

off_vm_weight (\(\lambda_{\text{off}}\), default 1.0). Pull of \(\hat V_i\) toward 0 on BFS-de-energised buses. Increase if the MAE of \(\hat V\) on de-energised buses plateaus above a few \(10^{-2}\) p.u.; decrease if energised-bus voltage error (VLD On Vm Loss) deteriorates, which indicates the shared trunk is being over-committed to the outage case.

on_vm_weight (\(\lambda_{\text{on}}\), default 0.5). Pull of \(\hat V_i\) toward the solver value on energised buses, weighted by the model's current confidence \(\hat p_i\). Because of that weighting it is weak early (when \(\hat p\) is uncertain) and strengthens as the classifier converges — a built-in curriculum. Keep below \(\lambda_{\text{off}}\); energised buses are the majority and already receive voltage supervision from the MaskedMSE/PBE terms outside this loss.

unreachable_l1_weight (\(\lambda_1\), default 1.0). Adds a constant pull of magnitude \(\lambda_1\lambda_{\text{off}}/n_{\text{off}}\) toward \(\hat V = 0\) on de-energised buses (eq. 24). The L2 part alone decays as \(\hat V \to 0\) and leaves a residual; the L1 part closes it. 1.0 means the constant pull equals the L2 pull at \(\hat V = 0.5\) p.u. Lower to 0.25–0.5 if de-energised voltages oscillate around zero (sign flips in the gradient at exactly 0).

docs.title: 3.2 Class balance — \(w_{\text{off}}\) of eq. (6)
docs.text:
unreachable_pos_weight (default auto). auto sets \(w_{\text{off}} = n_{\text{on}}/n_{\text{off}}\) from the BFS labels, so the de-energised minority contributes as much total gradient as the energised majority. A number fixes \(w_{\text{off}}\) (1.0 disables balancing). Use a number only when the outage rate is known and stable; auto adapts to each dataset and, with momentum, to each training phase.

max_pos_weight (default 10.0, previously 50.0). Upper clamp on \(w_{\text{off}}\). On the 33-bus N-3 set about 35–40 % of buses are de-energised, so \(w_{\text{off}} \approx 1.6\) and the clamp never binds. It protects sparse outage sets: at 50, a batch with one de-energised bus in 500 hands that bus ~9 % of the whole gradient and drives \(\theta\) to 0.02. Raise toward 20–30 only for large meshed networks where outages are genuinely rare, and watch VLD On Recall.

pos_weight_momentum (default 0.99, 0.0 = per-batch). EMA momentum for the auto weight; 0.99 is roughly a 100-batch window. Because \(\theta\) is derived from \(w_{\text{off}}\), a per-batch estimate would make the decision boundary jump between batches. The EMA is updated only in training mode and frozen for validation/test, and is saved with the checkpoint. Set to 0.0 to reproduce the original per-batch behaviour.

docs.title: 3.3 Reachability — eqs. (1)–(5)
docs.text:
reachability_sources (default ref). Which buses seed the BFS. ref = slack/ext_grid only, correct for IEEE-1547-style DG that trips on loss of mains (the 33-bus feeder). ref_and_gen also seeds from PV buses, i.e. treats islands with local generation as energised; only for grid-forming DG or intentional islanding studies. A wrong choice shows up directly as a high VLD Topo-vs-Target Disagreement.

input_state_threshold (\(\tau\), default 0.5). Threshold applied to the 0/1 status and contingency features. Leave at 0.5 unless the input pipeline rescales those columns (then the BFS will silently mislabel everything — check VLD Off Rate (labels) against the known outage rate on the first batch).

topology_confidence_gamma (\(\gamma\) of eq. 8, default 0.0). Down-weights the topology BCE on buses that are available but islanded (\(\alpha_i = 1,\ y_i^{\text{reach}} = 0\)) by \(e^{-\gamma}\). With correct labels these are exactly the buses VLD exists to detect, so down-weighting them works against the objective; 0 disables and is recommended. Kept for ablations.

docs.title: 4. Reading the training curves
docs.text:
Metric What it tells you Healthy sign VLD Off Recall / VLD Off Precision / VLD Off F1 Detection of de-energised buses (the task) F1 rising, precision not collapsing VLD On Recall \(1 -\) false-de-energisation rate \(\ge 0.97\) on the 33-bus set VLD Balanced Accuracy Mean of the two recalls; use for model selection Rising monotonically VLD Mean Prob (reachable & label 1) Calibration on unambiguous energised buses Near 1. If it sits near \(1/(1+w_{\text{off}})\), the class weight is the cause of a de-energisation bias VLD Decision Threshold \(1/(1+w_{\text{off}})\) in use Stable after the first ~100 batches VLD Off Class Weight \(w_{\text{off}}\) (EMA) \(\approx\) true on/off ratio, not pinned at the clamp VLD Topo-vs-Target Disagreement Fraction of conflict buses Low (< few %); persistent high values mean the BFS or the flags are wrong VLD Conflict Rate (reach 0, label 1) / (reach 1, label 0) Direction of the disagreement The first is the case that used to produce false de-energisations VLD Off Vm Loss / VLD On Vm Loss Voltage head on each class Both decreasing; On lags Off early by design

Rule of thumb for a de-energisation bias (On Recall low, Mean Prob low): check Off Class Weight first (clamp binding? lower max_pos_weight), then Conflict Rate (reach 0, label 1) (BFS missing paths? check reachability_sources), then target_anchor_weight.

docs.title: 5. Suggested sweep
docs.text:
The formulation fixes most of the behaviour; the two parameters that encode a real trade-off are

  • target_anchor_weight ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 1.0}
  • on_vm_weight ∈ {0.25, 0.5}

Select on validation VLD Balanced Accuracy, not VLD Off F1 (F1 on the off class is blind to false de-energisations). Six runs cover the grid.

docs.title: 6. Interaction with the other losses
docs.text: loss_weights: [0.05, 0.15, 0.80] for MaskedMSE, PBE, VLDTopologyLoss. PBE compares the injection implied by \(\hat V\) with the dataset's \(P_d, Q_d\). If the scenario generator leaves pre-contingency load on de-energised buses, PBE pulls \(\hat V\) up on exactly the buses \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{off}}\) pulls down. Either confirm loads are zeroed on de-energised buses in the data, mask PBE on those buses, or lower its weight.

docs.title: Contingency data generation
docs.text: contingency_data_gen is the data-generation application of this repository. It builds a pandapower network, enumerates N-1 … N-k contingencies (bus and branch outages), solves each post-contingency power flow and writes the results in the gridfm-datakit partitioned-parquet layout that gridfm_app_dist trains on.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
contingency_data_gen --config data_gen_1.yaml
gridfm_app_dist train --config configs/scenario_33radial.yaml --data_path data

Each scenario in the config produces <output_dir>/raw/{bus,gen,branch}_data.parquet, partitioned by scenario_partition = scenario // n_scenario_per_partition. With the shipped configs output_dir is data/<name>, so run from the repository root and point training at --data_path data.

docs.title: Config format
docs.text:
defaults:
  flag: 1                   # 1/2/3 Excel import method, 9 netlib YAML, 10 MATPOWER, null pandapower factory
  max_n_level: 3            # contingency depth: N-1 … N-max_n_level
  max_size: 500             # max memory per worker batch (MB); the scenario count per batch is derived from it
  n_scenario_per_partition: 200
  run_summary: true
  run_validation: true
  continue_on_error: true

scenarios:
  - name: case33radial
    network_file_path: networks/case33radial.xlsx
    flag: 1
    output_dir: data/scenario_33radial
    max_n_level: 3
  - name: urban_LV
    flag: 9
    builtin_network: netbuilder/urban_LV.yaml
    output_dir: data/scenario_urban_LV
  - name: cigre_lv
    flag: null
    builtin_network: create_cigre_network_lv
    output_dir: data/scenario_CIGRE_LV

Relative network_file_path / builtin_network values are resolved against the config file's directory first, then against the package configs/ folder and its networks/ and netbuilder/ sub-folders. A legacy ./config/ prefix is accepted.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
option meaning --config PATH\|NAME a YAML file, or the name of a shipped config (--list-configs) --only NAME … run a subset of the scenarios in the config --dry-run validate the config and report missing input files without running --list-configs list the configs shipped in contingency_data_gen/configs/

Worker count follows SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK (default 8).

docs.title: Package layout
docs.text:
module role contingency_data_gen.generation.scenario_data_gen ScenarioGenerator: contingency enumeration, parallel power flows, parquet output, validation contingency_data_gen.generation.datakit_extractors / datakit_writer gridfm-datakit column extraction and partitioned writing contingency_data_gen.generation.excel_pandapower* three Excel-to-pandapower import methods (flag 1/2/3) contingency_data_gen.netlib NetworkBuilder and the standard line/transformer type catalogue for YAML-defined MV/LV networks contingency_data_gen.configs shipped job configs, Excel networks (networks/), netlib network definitions (netbuilder/)

Network-builder examples and legacy comparison tools live in examples/datakit/.

docs.title: Integrating the Voltage-Loss-Detection (VLD) Task into gridfm-graphkit
docs.text: This document describes the changes made to gridfm-graphkit to integrate the new Voltage-Loss-Detection (VLD) task in the new (gridfm_app_dist) in the gridfm-app-distribution package is laid out.

docs.title: Task summary
docs.text: The VLD task teaches the heterogeneous GNS to predict, per bus, whether that bus remains energized after a set of component failures (contingencies), and to predict a consistent voltage magnitude for the energized buses. This turns the model into a topology-aware "will this bus stay live?" predictor on top of the existing power-flow reconstruction backbone.

docs.title: 1. New feature columns (datasets/globals.py)
docs.text:
The heterogeneous feature layout was extended. Base graphkit indices are kept; VLD adds four new indicators and repurposes the bus-output tail.

Bus input features (added):

Constant Index Meaning BUS_BASE_STATUS_H 15 Bus on/off status in the pre-contingency (base) topology BUS_CONT_H 16 Bus directly hit by a contingency (failure)

Branch / edge features (added):

Constant Index Meaning BRANCH_BASE_STATUS_E 11 Branch on/off status in the base topology BRANCH_CONT_E 12 Branch directly hit by a contingency

Bus output layout (changed for VLD). Base tasks emit [Vm, Va, Pg, Qg, Pd, Qd] (6 cols, PD_OUT=4, QD_OUT=5). The VLD model emits [Vm, Va, Pg, Qg, status_logit] (5 cols):

Constant Index Meaning PHYSICAL_BUS_DIM 4 Number of physical bus outputs [Vm, Va, Pg, Qg] BUS_STATUS_LOGIT_OUT 4 Column holding the predicted status logit BUS_STATUS_TARGET 5 Target column (energized/de-energized) in the target tensor

Important consequence. Because column 4 now means status logit (not Pd), any code that width-guards on size(1) > PD_OUT (4) would wrongly treat the status logit as a load-power column. This is why the normalizers and PBELoss were changed to guard on BUS_STATUS_TARGET (5) — see the code review, item 4.

docs.title: 2. New transforms (datasets/transforms.py, datasets/task_transforms.py)
docs.text:
• LoadGridParamsFromPathVLD — loads grid parameters plus base status and contingency indicators for buses and branches.
  • RemoveInactiveBranchesKeepTopology — drops electrically inactive branches for the physics computation while preserving the connectivity graph used for the reachability labels.
  • VoltageLossDetectionTransforms (registered under TRANSFORM_REGISTRY as "VoltageLossDetection") — the task Compose pipeline: LoadGridParamsFromPathVLD → RemoveInactiveBranchesKeepTopology → AddVLDHeteroMask.

docs.title: 3. New masking (datasets/masking.py)
docs.text: • AddVLDHeteroMask — produces the hetero mask dictionary for the VLD task, including the bus-status supervision mask.

docs.title: 4. New loss (training/loss.py)
docs.text:
• VLDTopologyLoss (registered "VLDTopologyLoss"). Objective = topology BCE + target-anchor BCE + off-bus Vm penalty + on-bus Vm penalty:
  • Reachability labels via _build_graph_reachability: iterative BFS from buses that are base-on and not contingency-hit, propagating over branches that are base-on and not contingency-hit — a direct encoding of the physical rule above.
  • Topology BCE trains the status logit against the hard reachability label, weighted by a confidence term exp(-γ·|bus_available − reachable|) that down-weights ambiguous buses.
  • Target-anchor BCE additionally anchors the logit to the supplied post-contingency status target.
  • Off-Vm loss drives predicted Vm → 0 on unreachable (de-energized) buses (L2 + weighted L1).
  • On-Vm loss matches predicted Vm to the target on reachable buses, scaled by the (detached) predicted status probability.
  • Configurable via loss_args: topology_weight, target_anchor_weight, off_vm_weight, on_vm_weight, unreachable_l1_weight, topology_confidence_gamma, input_state_threshold, prediction_threshold.
  • PBELoss ("PBE") and QgViolationPenaltyLoss ("QgViolationPenalty") carried from the reference and adapted to the VLD 6-argument loss call (they take x_dict=None and skip the shunt term when it is absent).

The loss reads topology from model.latest_x_dict["bus"] (stored by the GNS in its forward pass) rather than receiving x_dict as a call argument — see the interface note below.

docs.title: 5. New physics decoder (tasks/utils.py)
docs.text: • PhysicsDecoderVLD (registered "VoltageLossDetection" in PHYSICS_DECODER_REGISTRY) joins the existing PhysicsDecoderOPF/PF/SE. All four physics decoders are now registered in tasks/utils.py (moved out of models/utils.py to avoid a duplicate-key crash).

docs.title: 6. New task module (tasks/vld_task.py)
docs.text: • VoltageLossDetectionTask(ReconstructionTask) (registered "VoltageLossDetection" in TASK_REGISTRY). Adds VLD-specific test/predict metrics: status accuracy, off/on-bus Vm behaviour, and per-bus status probability outputs for downstream evaluation.

docs.title: 7. Model head (models/gnn_heterogeneous_gns.py)
docs.text: • The heterogeneous GNS gains a dedicated bus_status_head. When task == "VoltageLossDetection" the head's status_logit is concatenated to the physical bus outputs, yielding the 5-column VLD bus output. The model also stores latest_x_dict in its forward pass so the loss can recover the input topology.

docs.title: Loss ↔ task interface
docs.text:
The VLD shared_step calls the loss without x_dict (loss_fn(pred, target, edge_index, edge_attr, mask, model=self.model)), unlike the base graphkit 7-argument interface.

MixedLoss.forward was updated to match, and the carried-over base losses accept x_dict=None so they remain callable in this 6-argument path.

docs.title: Example configuration
docs.text:
See examples/config/vld_config.yaml. The key VLD settings are:

task:
  task_name: VoltageLossDetection
model:
  type: GNS_heterogeneous
  output_bus_dim: 5          # [Vm, Va, Pg, Qg, status_logit]
training:
  losses: ["VLDTopologyLoss"]
  loss_weights: [1.0]
  loss_args:
    - topology_weight: 1.0
      target_anchor_weight: 0.25
      off_vm_weight: 1.0
      on_vm_weight: 0.5
      unreachable_l1_weight: 1.0
      topology_confidence_gamma: 10.0
      input_state_threshold: 0.5
      prediction_threshold: 0.5

docs.title: VLD Colab tutorial
docs.text:
A hands-on notebook that generates contingency data for pandapower's case33bw, derives and tunes VLDTopologyLoss on a five-bus example, trains a small model and runs inference with a pre-trained checkpoint.

Notebook and companion files: examples/tutorial_vld/ (README).

Open examples/tutorial_vld/Tutorial_vld_colab.ipynb in Google Colab, select a T4 GPU runtime and run top to bottom.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The steps below mirror the README.

Create and activate a virtual environment (make sure you use the right python version = 3.10, 3.11 or 3.12. I highly recommend 3.12)

python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate

docs.title: For users
docs.text:
Install gridfm-app-distribution from PyPI

Install a released version when one becomes available:

pip install gridfm-app-distribution

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/gridfm/gridfm-app-distribution.git
cd gridfm-app-distribution
python -m venv .venv
pip install -e ".[dev,test]"

torch-scatter is a required dependency. It cannot be bundled in pyproject.toml because the correct wheel depends on your PyTorch and CUDA versions, so it must be installed separately.

Get PyTorch + CUDA version for torch-scatter

TORCH_CUDA_VERSION=$(python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__ + ('+cpu' if torch.version.cuda is None else ''))")

Install the correct torch-scatter wheel

pip install torch-scatter -f https://data.pyg.org/whl/torch-${TORCH_CUDA_VERSION}.html

For documentation generation and unit testing, install with the optional dev and test extras:

pip install "gridfm-app-distribution[dev,test]"

docs.title: CLI commands
docs.text:
Interface to train, fine-tune, evaluate, and run inference on GridFM models using YAML configs and MLflow tracking.

gridfm-dist-app <command> [OPTIONS]

Available commands:

  • train - Train a new model from scratch
  • finetune - Fine-tune an existing pre-trained model
  • evaluate - Evaluate model performance on a dataset
  • predict - Run inference and save predictions
  • benchmark - Benchmark train-dataloader iteration speed

docs.title: Training Models
docs.text: gridfm-dist-app train --config path/to/config.yaml

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Type Description Default --config str Required. Path to the training configuration YAML file. None --exp_name str MLflow experiment name. timestamp --run_name str MLflow run name. run --log_dir str MLflow tracking/logging directory. mlruns --data_path str Root dataset directory. data --compile [MODE] str Enable torch.compile mode. Valid values: default, reduce-overhead, max-autotune, max-autotune-no-cudagraphs. If flag is passed without a value, mode is default. None --bfloat16 flag Cast model to torch.bfloat16 (model.to(torch.bfloat16)). False --tf32 flag Enable TF32 on Ampere+ GPUs via torch.set_float32_matmul_precision("high"). False --dataset_wrapper str Registered dataset wrapper name (see DATASET_WRAPPER_REGISTRY), e.g. SharedMemoryCacheDataset. None --plugins list[str] Python packages to import for plugin registration, e.g. gridfm-dist-app_ee. [] --num_workers int Override data.workers from YAML. Use 0 to debug worker crashes. None --dataset_wrapper_cache_dir str Disk cache directory for dataset wrapper; cache is loaded from here when present and saved after first population. None --profiler str Enable Lightning profiler (simple, advanced, pytorch). None --compute_dc_ac_metrics flag Compute ground-truth AC/DC power balance metrics on the test split. False --mp_context str DataLoader multiprocessing start method (spawn, fork, forkserver). Defaults to PyTorch's automatic choice. On Linux, spawn is recommended for safety (CUDA + fork is unsafe); other choices emit a warning. None

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Standard Training:

gridfm-dist-app train --config examples/config/rural_MVLV_test.yaml --data_path examples/data

docs.title: Example with saved normalizer stats
docs.text:
When evaluating a model on a dataset, you can pass the normalizer statistics from the original training run to ensure the same normalization parameters are used:

gridfm-dist-app evaluate \
  --config examples/config/HGNS_PF_datakit_case118.yaml \
  --model_path mlruns/<experiment_id>/<run_id>/artifacts/model/best_model_state_dict.pt \
  --normalizer_stats mlruns/<experiment_id>/<run_id>/artifacts/stats/normalizer_stats.pt \
  --data_path data

Note: The --normalizer_stats flag only affects normalizers with fit_strategy = "fit_on_train" (e.g. HeteroDataMVANormalizer). Per-sample normalizers (HeteroDataPerSampleMVANormalizer) always recompute their statistics from the current dataset regardless of this flag.

docs.title: Benchmarking Dataloader Throughput
docs.text: gridfm-dist-app benchmark --config path/to/config.yaml

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
Argument Type Description Default --config str Required. Path to configuration YAML file. None --data_path str Root dataset directory. data --epochs int Number of epochs to iterate through the train dataloader. 3 --dataset_wrapper str Registered dataset wrapper name (see DATASET_WRAPPER_REGISTRY), e.g. SharedMemoryCacheDataset. None --dataset_wrapper_cache_dir str Directory for dataset wrapper disk cache. None --num_workers int Override data.workers from YAML. None --plugins list[str] Python packages to import for plugin registration. [] --mp_context str DataLoader multiprocessing start method (spawn, fork, forkserver). Defaults to PyTorch's automatic choice. On Linux, spawn is recommended for safety (CUDA + fork is unsafe); other choices emit a warning. None

Use built-in help for full command details:

gridfm-dist-app --help
gridfm-dist-app <command> --help

docs.title: YAML configuration reference
docs.text: Every experiment is driven by one YAML file in examples/config/.

docs.title: Full example (current style)
docs.text:
task:
  task_name: VoltageLossDetection
data:
  baseMVA: 100
  mask_value: 0.0
  normalization: HeteroDataMVANormalizer
  networks:
  - rural_MVLV_test
  scenarios:
  - 250000
  test_ratio: 0.1
  val_ratio: 0.1
  workers: 32
  split_by_load_scenario_idx: true
model:
  attention_head: 8
  edge_dim: 13
  hidden_size: 48
  input_bus_dim: 17
  input_gen_dim: 6
  output_bus_dim: 2
  output_gen_dim: 1
  num_layers: 12
  type: GNS_heterogeneous
optimizer:
  beta1: 0.9
  beta2: 0.999
  learning_rate: 0.0005
  lr_decay: 0.7
  lr_patience: 5
seed: 0
training:
  batch_size: 64
  epochs: 200
  loss_weights:
    - 0.1
    - 0.5
    - 0.4
  losses:
    - LayeredWeightedPhysics
    - MaskedBusMSE
    - VLDTopologyLoss
  loss_args:
    - { base_weight: 0.5 }
    - {}
    - {
        input_state_threshold: 0.5,
        prediction_threshold: 0.5,
        topology_weight: 1.0,
        target_anchor_weight: 0.25,
        off_vm_weight: 1.0,
        on_vm_weight: 0.5,
        unreachable_l1_weight: 1.0,
        topology_confidence_gamma: 10.0
      }
callbacks:
  patience: 100
  tol: 0

docs.title: Top-level keys
docs.text:
• task: task-specific settings (OptimalPowerFlow or PowerFlow).
  • data: dataset selection, normalization, splits, and loading behavior.
  • model: model architecture and dimensions.
  • optimizer: optimizer and scheduler parameters.
  • training: epochs, loss composition, and accelerator strategy.
  • callbacks: early stopping behavior.
  • seed: random seed used for reproducible shuffling/splits.
  • verbose: enables extra outputs (for example additional test plots/log artifacts).

docs.title: task.task_name
docs.text:
Task name registered in the framework:

  • VoltageLossDetection

docs.title: data.networks
docs.text: List of dataset folders under your data root. Examples: rural_MVLV, urban_MVLV, suburban_MVLV, semi-urban_MVLV.

docs.title: data.scenarios
docs.text: List of scenario counts, one value per network in data.networks. Example: with two networks, use two scenario entries in matching order.

docs.title: data.normalization
docs.text:
Normalizer class name:

  • HeteroDataMVANormalizer: fit one normalization scale from training data.
  • HeteroDataPerSampleMVANormalizer: fit per-scenario scales across the selected dataset.

docs.title: data.baseMVA
docs.text: Base MVA reference value (default in examples: 100). Used by normalizers for per-unit scaling.

docs.title: data.mask_value
docs.text: Fill value used when masking unavailable measurements/features (examples use 0.0).

docs.title: data.test_ratio, data.val_ratio
docs.text: Fractions for validation and test splits when split files are not supplied.

docs.title: data.workers
docs.text: Number of dataloader workers.

docs.title: data.split_by_load_scenario_idx
docs.text:
• true: split train/val/test by load scenario identifiers.
  • false: perform standard random split.

docs.title: data.split_from_existing_files
docs.text:
Optional path to precomputed split files. When provided:

  • split IDs are loaded from this folder,
  • data.scenarios is ignored for split construction,
  • do not combine with split_by_load_scenario_idx: true.

docs.title: model section
docs.text:
Current configs use the heterogeneous GNS model:

  • type: model registry name (examples use GNS_heterogeneous).
  • input_bus_dim: bus-node input feature dimension.
  • input_gen_dim: generator-node input feature dimension.
  • output_bus_dim: bus-node output dimension.
  • output_gen_dim: generator-node output dimension.
  • edge_dim: edge feature dimension.
  • hidden_size: hidden feature width.
  • num_layers: number of stacked message-passing layers.
  • attention_head: attention head count per layer.

docs.title: Core training controls
docs.text:
• batch_size: mini-batch size.
  • epochs: number of epochs.
  • accelerator: Lightning accelerator (auto, mps, cpu, gpu, etc.).
  • devices: Lightning device selection (auto, integer, list).
  • strategy: Lightning strategy (auto, ddp, etc.).

docs.title: Multi-loss configuration
docs.text:
• losses: list of registered loss names.
  • loss_weights: scalar weight per loss.
  • loss_args: list of argument objects matching losses by position.

All three lists must be aligned (same length and same order).

Registered loss names in current code:

  • LayeredWeightedPhysics
  • MaskedGenMSE
  • MaskedBusMSE
  • QgViolationPenalty
  • LossPerDim
  • MaskedMSE
  • MSE

Common loss_args patterns:

  • LayeredWeightedPhysics: {base_weight: <float>}
  • LossPerDim: {dim: VM|VA|P_in|Q_in, loss_str: MAE|MSE}
  • MaskedGenMSE, MaskedBusMSE, QgViolationPenalty, MaskedMSE, MSE: {}

docs.title: optimizer section
docs.text:
• learning_rate: initial learning rate.
  • beta1, beta2: Adam betas.
  • lr_decay: scheduler decay factor (e.g., ReduceLROnPlateau factor).
  • lr_patience: epochs to wait before applying LR decay.

docs.title: callbacks section
docs.text:
• patience: early stopping patience (epochs without sufficient improvement).
  • tol: minimum required improvement threshold to reset patience.

docs.title: Practical validation checklist
docs.text:
Before launching a run, verify:

  • len(data.networks) == len(data.scenarios).
  • len(training.losses) == len(training.loss_weights) == len(training.loss_args).
  • split_by_load_scenario_idx and split_from_existing_files are not both active.
